newsitem.title: UK: Dead stowaway found in wheel bay of British jet.
newsitem.headline: Dead stowaway found in wheel bay of British jet.

text.p: British Airways launched an immediate investigation on Sunday after the body of a boy was found in the wheel compartment of a Boeing 747 passenger plane that arrived from Nairobi.
"We've launched an investigation and are liaising with the highest autorities in Kenya," Bob Ayling, BA's chairman said in a statement.
"This is another human tragedy which we very much regret. Safety and security is important to British Airways and we take this incident very seriously," he added.
Ground staff found the boy, described by police as "of African appearance", at Gatwick Airport near London on Sunday. His body was taken to a nearby hospital where an autopsy will be performed.
"This was a tragic loss of a young life and one can only guess at what spurred him into doing something so dangerous," Police Inspector Peter Cooper said.
It was second incident of stowaways being found in the wheel compartments of BA jets in less than six months.
Pardeep Saini, 22, was found wandering on the tarmac at Londons Heathrow last October after he survived a 10-hour flight from India to Britain in the wheel hold at temperatures of -60C (-76F).
His younger brother Vijay, 19, froze to death during the same flight and his body fell to the ground as the jet's wheels were lowered on its landing approach.

Doctors said it was nothing short of a miracle that Saini had survived the flight in the harsh conditions. They think he probably lost consciousness and went into a state of suspended animation which helped to prevent brain damage.
The two men fled the Punjab after being accused of being supporters of Sikh separatists, which they denied.
A BA spokeswoman said the airline was particularly concerned by the way the stowaways from both Kenya and India had apparently gained access to the aircraft when they were in secure areas.
She said the airline was contacting the British Foreign Office and the Department of Transport to discuss ways to prevent other similar incidents.
